test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 12 Dec 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Raghav purchased a shirt at Rs. 1,500 and marked up the price of the shirt by 40%. What is the discount percentage he has to offer in order to get a profit of Rs. 75?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume Cost Price (CP) = 100%, then Marked Price (MP) = 100% + 40% = 140%.

Profit % on CP = (75 ÷ 1500) × 100 = 5% ⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 105%.

Discount is given on MP, so Discount = MP − SP = 140% − 105% = 35%.

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (35 ÷ 140) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹1500

Markup = 40%

Profit = ₹75

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit

Discount % = ((MP − SP) ÷ MP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/309c39235d836e7c5efc978bf9e79cd11cf0f03a92a6e8631a73a44e9f1ebd71.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP = 1500 × (1 + 40 ÷ 100) = 1500 × 1.4 = ₹2100

⇒ SP = 1500 + 75 = ₹1575

⇒ Discount = MP − SP = 2100 − 1575 = ₹525

⇒ Discount % = (525 ÷ 2100) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) & Discount

MP is the price printed or tagged on an article. Discounts are always calculated on the MP unless stated otherwise. The formula is: SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given on an article, the equivalent single discount given is (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100)%.

Direct CP to MP Ratio

The direct ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price can be quickly written as CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).
